Does your Sdn Bhd need to be audited?

Most Malaysian private companies must have their financial statements audited each year by a licensed company auditor. The Companies Act 2016 lets certain companies — for example dormant companies and small, threshold-qualified private companies — claim an exemption. Whether yours qualifies depends on its revenue, assets and other conditions, so we check your eligibility before recommending an audit. Read our guide: Does my Sdn Bhd need an audit?

What a statutory audit involves

  • Planning — we agree the timetable backwards from your SSM and LHDN deadlines.
  • Preparation — we confirm your schedules, bank confirmations and supporting documents are ready.
  • Fieldwork — the audit of balances and transactions, with clear queries rather than surprises.
  • Reporting — the audited financial statements and auditor’s report for directors to sign and for lodging with SSM.
  • Management feedback — practical recommendations on internal controls and bookkeeping.

Audit deadlines to plan around

StepDeadline
Circulate audited accounts to membersWithin 6 months of financial year end
Lodge audited accounts with SSMWithin 30 days of circulation
File Form C with LHDNWithin 7 months of financial year end

Because the Form C relies on finalised accounts, an audit that finishes late pushes your tax filing late too. Using the same team for bookkeeping, audit coordination and tax keeps every deadline aligned.

FAQ

Audit questions

Which Malaysian companies are exempt from audit?

Certain dormant companies and small, threshold-qualified private companies may be exempt under the Companies Act 2016. We check your figures and conditions before advising.

How long does a statutory audit take?

It depends on the size and the state of your books. Companies with current monthly bookkeeping are audited faster, which is why we plan the audit from the start of the year.

Can the firm doing my bookkeeping also do my audit?

Independence rules apply. We coordinate the audit and make sure the right licensed professionals handle each role, so your books and audit stay aligned.

What happens if we lodge audited accounts late?

SSM can impose compounds on the company and its officers. We can help you catch up and regularise overdue lodgements.
